_note: Every visible string of the release universe (universe.html, assets/universe.js). Built by scripts/build_universe.py. Plain words; numbers are filled in from the data at build time or in the page.

page.title: The release universe
page.description: Every family of OpenAI’s mathematics release as its own small map, placed by discipline, with the citations between families drawn as fibres. Drill into a family to see its papers, headline results and Lean statements.
page.lede: Each of the {families} families is a small map of its own papers, headline results and Lean statements, set in its discipline’s sector. Fibres in the middle are the citations between families.
page.noscript: The interactive map needs JavaScript. The list below names every family, paper, headline result and Lean statement, with links.

controls.canvas_label: Map of the release: {families} families in {disciplines} discipline sectors. Use the list beside it for the same objects as links.
controls.help: Select a family to light its citations and fly into its map. Double-click opens a page. Esc goes back. Scroll or pinch over the map to zoom.

search.label: Find a theorem or a Lean declaration
search.placeholder: Find a theorem or a Lean declaration
search.failed: The search index could not load. The list below names every object.
search.count: {n} matches. Enter flies to the first.

legend.heading: How to read the map
legend.colour_note: Colour marks evidence only. Structure stays grey.
legend.lean_3: Re-run and accepted by three outside groups
legend.lean_holes: Has definitions Comparator checks by name and type only (a hole)
legend.pair_note: Pairings are chosen automatically by word overlap and have not been reviewed.
legend.family_hol: Some steps checked again in HOL Light
legend.family_finite: A finite part checked by exact computation
legend.fibre_note: A fibre joins two families when a manuscript of one cites a manuscript of the other. Its width grows with the number of citing links.

release.heading: The release
release.summary: {families} families in {disciplines} disciplines: {papers} current papers, {results} headline results and {lean} Lean statements.
release.index_intro: Every family, its papers, their headline results and its Lean statements, by discipline. Each line links to its page.

discipline.connections: Citing links with families in other disciplines: {out} outward, {in} inward.

family.no_connections: No manuscript in this family cites or is cited by another family’s manuscript.
family.readers_heading: Do the two outside readers agree?
family.readers_source: MathVet and Carlos Toledo’s cert-machine each read the family’s Lean statements against its headline, independently of each other.
family.readers_agree-full: Both find the Lean states the headline.
family.readers_agree-less: Both find the Lean states less than the headline.
family.readers_none: No Lean statement is linked to this family, so there is nothing to read against the headline.
family.hol: Ben Knill checked {n} of its steps again in HOL Light.
family.hol_one: Ben Knill checked one of its steps again in HOL Light.
family.finite: Carlos Toledo’s cert-machine checked {n} finite parts by exact computation.
family.finite_one: Carlos Toledo’s cert-machine checked one finite part by exact computation.
family.finite_other: {n} more finite parts were looked at and not decided.
family.findings_none: No credited finding about this family yet.

paper.no_results: The atlas found no headline statement in this paper’s TeX source.

result.paired: Paired with {names}. The pairing was chosen automatically by word overlap and has not been reviewed.
result.unpaired: No Lean statement is paired with this result.
result.load_failed: The statement could not load. Read it in the paper instead.
result.numbering_note: Numbers are those of the atlas’s reading page, computed from the TeX source; the PDF is authoritative.

lean.reruns_none: No outside group has re-run this file yet.
lean.holes_heading: Definitions checked by name and type only
lean.holes_note: Comparator compares these by name and type; their bodies must be read in OpenAI’s library.
lean.paired_note: Chosen automatically by word overlap; not reviewed.
lean.paired_none: No paper result is paired with it.
lean.main: In OpenAI’s list of main results
